input.title: Accept the rupee sign (₹) in parseAmount
input.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

parseAmount strips whitespace and a fixed set of currency symbols (€$£¥) before validating the amount, but it is missing ₹, so rupee-prefixed amounts like `₹1,250.00` fail to parse and are reported as "not a number". Add ₹ (and ideally any non-digit currency-sign characters generally) to the stripped character set in parseAmount so INR amounts import correctly.

label: bug
file: src/util/money.ts

parseAmount only strips a fixed set of currency symbols (€$£¥) from the raw text before validating it as a number. The rupee sign ₹ isn't in that set, so `₹1,250.00` fails the numeric regex and is rejected as "not a number", even though the same parser handles euro/dollar/pound amounts with a sign. Adding ₹ to the stripped characters (and more generally handling other currency signs/prefixes such as the Swiss "CHF" and the apostrophe thousands separator mentioned in the discussion) would fix this.
